```js
if (playerAction.type === 'switch' || playerAction.type === 'item' || playerAction.type === 'struggle' && false) {
```

The `&& false` part effectively disables the `'struggle'` branch, but it also makes the whole condition a bit confusing. Moreover, the precedence of `&&` over `||` means the condition actually evaluates as:

```js
if (playerAction.type === 'switch' ||
    playerAction.type === 'item' ||
    (playerAction.type === 'struggle' && false)) {
```

So `'struggle'` will never be true, which is probably intentional because struggle is handled elsewhere, but the extra `&& false` is a hacky way to comment it out. Since struggle is a forced move when a Pokémon has no other moves, it should be processed in the normal attack handling path, not here. Therefore, the cleanest fix is to remove the `'struggle' && false` clause entirely, leaving only the genuinely relevant action types.
